blocks.tex: For adjacent-unequal words, plateau extrema reduce to strict local extrema. The following lemmas are the finite combinatorial inputs used in selecting the four active edges.

blocks.label: lem:n6mr_max_run_len_zero
blocks.title: an adjacent-unequal word has no nontrivial plateau maximum
blocks.body:
If $f_i \ne f_{i+1}$ for every $i$ and $\mathrm{PlateauMaxRun}\,f\,a\,k$
  holds, then $k = 0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.PlateauMaxRun.eq_zero_of_ne_succ
lean.code:
lemma PlateauMaxRun.eq_zero_of_ne_succ {n : ℕ} {f : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hne : ∀ i, f i ≠ f (i + 1)) {a k : ℕ} (h : PlateauMaxRun f a k) :
    k = 0 := by
  by_contra hk
  have hk1 : 1 ≤ k := Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr hk
  have hc := h.1 1 hk1
  rw [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one] at hc
  exact hne (a : ZMod n) hc.symm

blocks.tex:
Suppose $k \ge 1$.  The constancy clause at $m = 1$ gives
  $f(a + 1) = f(a)$, contradicting the adjacent-inequality hypothesis at
  $i = a$.

blocks.label: lem:n6mr_max_run_strict
blocks.title: a plateau maximum of an adjacent-unequal word is strict
blocks.body:
If $f_i \ne f_{i+1}$ for every $i$ and $\mathrm{PlateauMaxRun}\,f\,a\,k$
  holds, then the residue of $a$ is a strict local maximum of $f$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.PlateauMaxRun.isStrictLocalMax_of_ne_succ
lean.code:
lemma PlateauMaxRun.isStrictLocalMax_of_ne_succ {n : ℕ} {f : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hne : ∀ i, f i ≠ f (i + 1)) {a k : ℕ} (h : PlateauMaxRun f a k) :
    IsStrictLocalMax f (a : ZMod n) := by
  have hk := h.eq_zero_of_ne_succ hne
  subst k
  exact ⟨h.2.1, by simpa [Nat.cast_add] using h.2.2⟩

deps.title: an adjacent-unequal word has no nontrivial plateau maximum
deps.label: lem:n6mr_max_run_len_zero

blocks.tex:
By \cref{lem:n6mr_max_run_len_zero} the run has $k = 0$, so its two strict
  drops read $f(a - 1) < f(a)$ and $f(a + 1) < f(a)$, which is
  \cref{def:zz_local_max} verbatim.

blocks.title: Strict extrema forced by a four-vertex window

blocks.label: thm:n6mr_two_strict_max
blocks.title: a window gives two distinct strict local maxima
blocks.body:
Let $\mathrm{DFV}(w; c)$ hold and let $w_i \ne w_{i+1}$ for every $i$.
  Then there are $i \ne j$ in $\ZMod n$, both strict local maxima of $w$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.DFV.exists_two_strictLocalMax
lean.code:
theorem DFV.exists_two_strictLocalMax {n : ℕ} {w : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    (h : DFV w c) (hne : ∀ i, w i ≠ w (i + 1)) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ IsStrictLocalMax w i ∧ IsStrictLocalMax w j := by
  obtain ⟨a, k, b, l, _hk, _hl, ha, hb, hab⟩ := h.plateau_extrema.1
  have hk0 := ha.eq_zero_of_ne_succ hne
  have hl0 := hb.eq_zero_of_ne_succ hne
  subst k
  subst l
  refine ⟨(a : ZMod n), (b : ZMod n), ?_,
    ha.isStrictLocalMax_of_ne_succ hne, hb.isStrictLocalMax_of_ne_succ hne⟩
  simpa using hab 0 (by omega) 0 (by omega)

deps.title: the DFV window meets Dahlberg's conclusion class --- wrapped form
deps.label: cor:dfv_plateau_extrema_window

deps.label: lem:n6mr_max_run_len_zero

deps.title: a plateau maximum of an adjacent-unequal word is strict
deps.label: lem:n6mr_max_run_strict

blocks.tex:
\cref{cor:dfv_plateau_extrema_window} supplies two plateau maximum runs
  $(a, k)$ and $(b, l)$ together with the disjointness clause.  By
  \cref{lem:n6mr_max_run_len_zero} both run lengths are $0$, so the
  disjointness clause instantiated at $m_1 = m_2 = 0$ says exactly that the
  residues of $a$ and $b$ differ; and \cref{lem:n6mr_max_run_strict} makes
  each of them a strict local maximum.
